key_insight: Higher-order QMC–Galerkin finite element error bounds remain robust as the perturbation parameter ε becomes small, with constants independent of parameter dimension.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports uncertainty quantification for reaction–diffusion models with thin boundary layers without deterioration of error constants as ε decreases.
method: Establish ε-uniform stability and mixed-parametric regularity in a weighted energy norm.
Combine dimension truncation and higher-order QMC integration for linear quantities of interest.
Couple spatial error estimates with QMC analysis; verify robust approximation using 1D Shishkin-mesh FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments illustrate predicted robustness and convergence rates, while robust spatial approximation is verified for a one-dimensional model with continuous piecewise affine elements.
watch_item: The general fully discrete guarantee assumes ε-robust finite element approximation, explicitly verified here only for a one-dimensional model.
paper_title: Higher-Order QMC Galerkin FEM for Singular Perturbation: Reaction-Diffusion with Affine-Parametric Reaction
